content:
morgan: :rotating_light: incidents-bot sent a spike alert - prod 500s up ~6% over baseline. Seeing errors from inference API. Root cause unknown, starting thread.
morgan: stacktrace looks like model-serving process failing on startup with `cannot open shared library` errors. 
incidents-bot: Alert: prod-inference service 5xx rate increased (6m avg) - triggered at 1902501234.
deploy-bot: Deploy started by @alex: image=registry.redwood.io/inference:2026-03-15-8f2d7a sha=sha256:deadbeef tag=canary-20260315  (canary->50%)
alex: I rolled a canary at ~1902501200, monitor looked ok for the first 10m but error spike shows up ~1902501230.
rebecca: Can anyone confirm whether canary health checks passed? I see failed liveness on a subset of nodes.
ian: grabbing kube events + pod logs now. short term: increase replicas on stable?
sanjay: looking at image layers: the canary image layer 4 seems to be a different glibc build than expected. `ldd` failing on startup. Could be a cache-hit in our CI that reused an older base layer.
morgan: if base mismatch -> feature binary built against one libc but runtime has another -> segfaults. Immediate mitigation: kill canary rollout and rollback to previous image. Can someone flip feature flag to disable model-autoload fallback?
alex: flipping rollout to 0% and promoting stable. `deploy-bot rollback inference canary-20260315 --to image=inference:2026-03-14-af3c1b`
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by @alex -> target image inference:2026-03-14-af3c1b. Canary traffic shifting to stable.
rebecca: feature flag `model_autoload_v2` set to false (kill-switch) to avoid noisy restarts. :white_check_mark:
ian: pods from canary are draining, new stable pods coming up. still seeing a small tail of 500s from a few regions.
sanjay: CI pipeline step `docker:cache:layer-restore` probably pulled a stale layer from our artifact cache. I can see the offending layer digest: sha256:badlayer123 (not expected).
morgan: ok we need a fix in CI and an incident action now: 1) purge layer from registry cache 2) force rebuild without cache 3) validate base layer sha before tagging 4) improve canary health gating 
alex: triggering registry garbage action: `registryctl purge-layer sha256:badlayer123 --scope=inference`
sanjay: re-running build with `--no-cache` now and will push `inference:2026-03-15-8f2d7a-rebuild` with verified base sha. Command: ```docker build --no-cache -t registry.redwood.io/inference:2026-03-15-8f2d7a-rebuild . && docker push registry.redwood.io/inference:2026-03-15-8f2d7a-rebuild```
rebecca: heads up to support: some customers in EU saw 10-15% errors between 1902501205-1902501250. Please prepare incident message for impacted customers once rollback completes.
ian: rolling back increased success rate. 5xxs dropping to baseline. network traces look clean.
morgan: confirm oncall handoff: I'm taking the incident until 1902502000, then handing over to @ian. Leave notes in the incident doc.
incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-17, severity=P2.
sanjay: registry purge completed. pushed rebuilt image with verified base sha `sha256:cleanbase999`.
deploy-bot: New canary push: registry.redwood.io/inference:2026-03-15-8f2d7a-rebuild -> starting canary 5%
rebecca: running smoke / health checks: OK on US, EU, APAC. Observability shows mean latency stable.
ian: canary at 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 15m window with no regression.
alex: promoting rebuilt image to stable now.
deploy-bot: Promotion complete. All traffic on inference service now at inference:2026-03-15-8f2d7a-rebuild.
morgan: support update drafted: "We've rolled back a faulty canary, rebuilt images without cache, and promoted a validated image. Customers in EU may have experienced intermittent 500s for ~5 minutes; no data loss. Working on postmortem."
rebecca: :eyes: please include list of affected customer orgs and whether any SLA credit applies.
ian: I've attached brief logs to the incident doc and set a follow-up eval: regress test for libc mismatch.
sanjay: follow-ups: add base-layer digest check to CI (fail build if base differs), add automated registry cache invalidation step on base updates, and tighten canary health gating.
morgan: agreed. also add runbook step: if canary fails with shared-lib errors, kill feature flag + rollback + purge layer.
rebecca: thanks team. I'll notify CS and ops to contact affected customers.
morgan: handing over to @ian at 1902502000 for monitoring and postmortem draft. If anything reappears ping here. :hammer_and_wrench:
ian: I'll own postmortem and follow-ups. tagging this thread for the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
